 THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 12.02.2019 PASSED IN MVC NO.7817/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE III ADDITIONAL JUDGE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES, MACT,
BENGALURU (SCCH-18), AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.12,44,000/- WITH INTEREST AT 8 PER CENT P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL THE DATE OF DEPOSIT.

THIS MFA COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The insurer is in appeal challenging the award of Rs.12,44,000/- granted for death of Sekh Nafazul, a 20 years old.

2. The insurer is contending that the deceased suffered serious injuries when the tipper lorry unloaded the crushed stone sand and since the deceased was outside the vehicle, it could not be considered as an accident arising out of the use of the motor vehicle.
It is also contended that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess a driving licence and therefore, the insurance company could not be made liable.
3. It is not in dispute that the accident occurred because of use of the hydraulic power bucket, which was raised to unload the crushed stone sand.
Since the bucket was a part of the motor vehicle and the death occurred when it was lifted to unload the vehicle, it has to be held that it was an accident arising out of the use of a motor vehicle.

In such cases, whether the deceased was inside the vehicle or outside the vehicle would make no difference and if the accident occurred due to the use of the motor vehicle, then the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act would apply.
M/S. Reliance

General Insurance vs Anowara Bibi on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50786500/
2 4.

As far as the second contention that the driver of the vehicle did not possess a valid driving licence is concerned, the officials from the Transport Department were examined and they stated that the driver of the offending vehicle did possess the driving licence.
The Tribunal has relied upon this evidence to come to the conclusion that the insurer would be liable.

Reliance placed on the charge-sheet, which indicates that the driver was charged with driving the vehicle without licence,
cannot be accepted in light of the deposition of the officials of the RTO.
Thus, there is no merit in the appeal filed by the insurer and the same is dismissed.
5. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal for disbursal in terms of the award.
